messages.text: Please explain in simple language what stopped the last attempt and how we can continue.

Here's exactly what happened, in plain terms — two separate snags, and only one is about the copy itself:

1. The code never reached me. You sent the link, which is the right address — but a link is just an address. From where I sit I can't open it and look inside; the only thing I can see is what's typed or pasted right into this chat. So I had the envelope, not the letter. And I won't invent code and call it a copy — a made-up file is worse than no file.
2. My note-saving hit a bump. When I tried to record where things stood, the storage answered "409 conflict" — meaning the copy it holds was newer than the one I'd started from, so it refused my save rather than risk overwriting something. That error message you saw was the safety catch doing its job. Nothing was lost and my notes are intact.

Getting unstuck takes about a minute:
1. Open chat-test.html anywhere you can see its raw code (its GitHub page works).
2. Select everything and copy it.
3. Paste it straight into this chat as a plain message — all of it, no matter how long.

The moment the real code is in front of me, I'll write it word-for-word into the new file and leave the original completely untouched. One small thing to settle when you paste: earlier you typed "bugsbunnny.html" with three n's — let me know whether the new file should be exactly that, or bugsbunny.html with two.
